lem-maximal-ode-solution-extends-from-co.empty: Statement d>=1 and t0<b give at least one coordinate and a nonempty time segment; its graph in C also makes the compact tube nonempty.
lem-maximal-ode-solution-extends-from-co.zero: Proof step 1.1 permits M=0, giving constant coordinates; step 2.1 divides only by n+1>0 and step 3.1 only by b-t>0.
lem-maximal-ode-solution-extends-from-co.one: Proof step 1.1 sums finitely many coordinate bounds and works with exactly one coordinate when d=1.
lem-maximal-ode-solution-extends-from-co.degenerate: Proof step 3.1 treats both b in I and b outside I before gluing; a constant trajectory or zero field still has the endpoint extension.
lem-maximal-ode-solution-extends-from-co.endpoints: Proof steps 2.1 and 3.1 construct xb at the finite right endpoint and match the left derivative to the local solution's right derivative.
lem-maximal-ode-solution-extends-from-co.nonempty-choice: Proof step 2.1 prescribes tn=b-(b-t0)/(n+1); the coordinate limits and one local endpoint IVP require no selector over an arbitrary family.
lem-maximal-ode-solution-extends-from-co.iff-forward: The compact-tube lemma rules out one finite-endpoint configuration for a maximal solution; it asserts no equivalence between boundedness and global existence.
lem-maximal-ode-solution-extends-from-co.iff-reverse: No converse says that every globally extendible solution remains in a particular compact tube; the assertion is only the stated extension obstruction.

thm-ode-residual-a-posteriori-error-boun.empty: Statement d>=1 and a<b exclude an empty coordinate family and an empty time interval in the absolutely-continuous residual estimate.
thm-ode-residual-a-posteriori-error-boun.zero: Proof step 2.1 divides by q only where q>0 and proves q'=0 at differentiability points with q=0; step 5.1 divides by strictly positive w(t).
thm-ode-residual-a-posteriori-error-boun.one: Proof step 1.1's finite coordinate argument works for d=1, with epsilon/d=epsilon and one absolute-continuity threshold.
thm-ode-residual-a-posteriori-error-boun.degenerate: Proof steps 2.1 and 5.1 admit zero residual envelope and zero initial error; the bound then forces zero reconstruction error rather than dividing by it.
thm-ode-residual-a-posteriori-error-boun.endpoints: Proof step 5.1 applies the absolutely-continuous FTC on [a,t] and uses w(a)=1; at t=a the estimate reduces to the initial error itself.
thm-ode-residual-a-posteriori-error-boun.nonempty-choice: Statement explicitly assumes Countable Choice and Dependent Choice; proof steps 2.1 and 5.1 retain the almost-everywhere and absolutely-continuous FTC suppliers under those axioms.
thm-ode-residual-a-posteriori-error-boun.iff-forward: The residual theorem deduces an error upper bound from a one-sided Lipschitz inequality and an actual residual envelope; it states no characterization of all accurate reconstructions.
thm-ode-residual-a-posteriori-error-boun.iff-reverse: A small reconstruction error is not asserted to provide the residual hypothesis or justify an embedded-pair estimator; the final Statement sentence expressly separates that issue.

thm-piecewise-c1-ode-residual-a-posterio.empty: Statement a<T requires at least one finite partition panel and d>=1 requires at least one state component.
thm-piecewise-c1-ode-residual-a-posterio.zero: Proof step 1.1 uses q_epsilon=sqrt(||e||^2+epsilon^2)>0, so zero error causes no division; step 3.1 takes epsilon down to zero only after integration.
thm-piecewise-c1-ode-residual-a-posterio.one: Proof step 2.1 sums finitely many panel inequalities and allows a partition with just one panel; no internal cancellation is needed in that case.
thm-piecewise-c1-ode-residual-a-posterio.degenerate: Proof step 1.1 permits ell=0 and rho=0, and step 3.1's limit remains valid when either error norm vanishes.
thm-piecewise-c1-ode-residual-a-posterio.endpoints: Proof step 2.1 integrates full or partial panels and cancels neighboring endpoint terms by continuity, covering partition nodes and both horizon endpoints.
thm-piecewise-c1-ode-residual-a-posterio.nonempty-choice: The Statement restricts to finite-piece ordinary calculus and explicitly claims no choice axiom; proof step 2.1 adds only a finite list of panel inequalities.
thm-piecewise-c1-ode-residual-a-posterio.iff-forward: This finite-piece theorem is an integrating-factor upper estimate under supplied reconstruction and residual hypotheses, with no necessary-and-sufficient assertion.
thm-piecewise-c1-ode-residual-a-posterio.iff-reverse: It does not recover a piecewise-C1 reconstruction or a residual envelope from a known error bound; the general absolutely-continuous direction is a separate result.

def-embedded-runge-kutta-pair-and-error-.empty: Definition stages run in explicit tableau order; for the first stage the sum over j<i is empty and contributes zero, leaving f(tn+c1h,yn).
def-embedded-runge-kutta-pair-and-error-.zero: Definition E_n(h) is the Euclidean norm of the high-low difference, so identical pair outputs give E_n(h)=0 without a division or a reliability assertion.
def-embedded-runge-kutta-pair-and-error-.one: Definition uses the Euclidean norm on d>=1 states; for a scalar state the estimator is the absolute value of the same two output values.
def-embedded-runge-kutta-pair-and-error-.degenerate: Definition explicitly separates computation of the embedded difference from any bound on either local defect; coincident outputs or a vanishing leading error are not declared reliable.
def-embedded-runge-kutta-pair-and-error-.endpoints: Definition fixes a single step start tn and produces two endpoint values; it supplies no closed time-horizon or final-step clipping rule.
def-embedded-runge-kutta-pair-and-error-.nonempty-choice: The common tableau weights determine both finite weighted outputs and their difference; no arbitrary minimizer or nonempty-set selector is introduced.
def-embedded-runge-kutta-pair-and-error-.iff-forward: The embedded-pair definition specifies shared stages and two weight vectors and defines a computed norm; it asserts no logical equivalence about estimator reliability.
def-embedded-runge-kutta-pair-and-error-.iff-reverse: Estimator equality or a small computed norm is not claimed to imply either member's local order or an error-bound hypothesis.

alg-bounded-adaptive-runge-kutta-control.empty: Definition initializes the accepted mesh with (t0,y0), even before any attempt; zero accepted steps do not produce an empty returned mesh.
alg-bounded-adaptive-runge-kutta-control.zero: Definition step5 explicitly selects gamma_max when Q=0 and uses the positive root only when Q>0; step3 scales by atol+rtol*max>=atol>0.
alg-bounded-adaptive-runge-kutta-control.one: Definition's positive integer attempt budget admits N=1; step4 terminal success/minimum-step tests precede the final step5 budget return.
alg-bounded-adaptive-runge-kutta-control.degenerate: Definition step2 returns failure for domain, undefined or nonfinite stage/output arithmetic; rejected trials preserve the accepted prefix rather than creating a spurious endpoint.
alg-bounded-adaptive-runge-kutta-control.endpoints: Definition returns immediate success when t0=T, clips the final step by T-t, and tests reaching T before budget exhaustion.
alg-bounded-adaptive-runge-kutta-control.nonempty-choice: Tableau order, scalar maxima/minima, the specified positive root and explicit status branches determine the finite controller; no unrestricted selector is required.
alg-bounded-adaptive-runge-kutta-control.iff-forward: This adaptive controller defines an acceptance test Q<=1 and statuses; it does not equate acceptance with global accuracy or stiffness detection.
alg-bounded-adaptive-runge-kutta-control.iff-reverse: Actual small ODE error does not imply this controller accepts a trial, and an embedded difference alone is expressly not an a posteriori certificate.

def-heun-euler-embedded-runge-kutta-pair.empty: Definition prescribes exactly two stages K1,K2 and two output formulas; no zero-stage pair is part of this Euler-Heun construction.
def-heun-euler-embedded-runge-kutta-pair.zero: Definition gives YH-YE=h(K2-K1)/2, so equal stage values or a zero step yield a zero embedded difference without a reciprocal of that difference.
def-heun-euler-embedded-runge-kutta-pair.one: Definition permits a scalar ODE; the same K1,K2 and high/low weights apply with one state coordinate.
def-heun-euler-embedded-runge-kutta-pair.degenerate: Definition states local orders are proved separately, so a zero field or identical outputs only instantiate the formulas and do not themselves certify order or estimator reliability.
def-heun-euler-embedded-runge-kutta-pair.endpoints: Definition evaluates K1 at tn and K2 at tn+h; no independent mesh-horizon convention is included in this pair definition.
def-heun-euler-embedded-runge-kutta-pair.nonempty-choice: Both explicit function evaluations and the fixed weights (1/2,1/2),(1,0) prescribe the pair; no arbitrary choice is made.
def-heun-euler-embedded-runge-kutta-pair.iff-forward: The Euler-Heun item defines particular stage/output values, rather than proving a biconditional characterization of all embedded pairs.
def-heun-euler-embedded-runge-kutta-pair.iff-reverse: A difference of the form h(K2-K1)/2 is not asserted to identify a unique tableau or imply the separately proved local orders.

prop-embedded-pair-estimator-asymptotics.empty: Statement fixes one IVP and one initial state, not a possibly empty collection over which a uniform conclusion is selected.
prop-embedded-pair-estimator-asymptotics.zero: Proof step 2.1 divides asymptotic defects only when ||a||>0; for a=0 it computes the t^2 Euler-Heun ratio 3/2 and also gives an identically zero estimator example.
prop-embedded-pair-estimator-asymptotics.one: Proof step 2.1 includes the scalar t^2 IVP, where the stated asymptotic reasoning has one coordinate and the exact endpoint is h^3/3.
prop-embedded-pair-estimator-asymptotics.degenerate: Statement and proof step 2.1 explicitly separate the vanishing leading coefficient from the ratio-one conclusion, retaining the zero-field counterexample to positive estimator size.
prop-embedded-pair-estimator-asymptotics.endpoints: Statement is a limit as h decreases to zero through positive h; proof step 2.1 divides by h^(p+1) only on that punctured positive-step domain.
prop-embedded-pair-estimator-asymptotics.nonempty-choice: Proof step 1.1 subtracts two given defect expansions and step 2.1 takes their scalar norm limits; no family of solution selectors is used.
prop-embedded-pair-estimator-asymptotics.iff-forward: The asymptotic proposition gives ratio one when a is nonzero and warns about a=0; it does not claim that ratio one characterizes a nonzero leading coefficient.
prop-embedded-pair-estimator-asymptotics.iff-reverse: No reverse inference from the numerical ratio to the assumed defect expansions is made; zero leading terms may have other ratios or zero denominators.

def-heun-quadratic-dense-output.empty: Definition constructs one polynomial from one Heun step and its two stages; an absent panel or missing stage is not an input to this construction.
def-heun-quadratic-dense-output.zero: Definition P_n(theta)=yn+h(theta K1+theta^2(K2-K1)/2) involves no division by the stage difference, so a zero field or equal stages is allowed.
def-heun-quadratic-dense-output.one: Definition is componentwise and remains the same scalar quadratic when the ODE has one component.
def-heun-quadratic-dense-output.degenerate: Definition labels the polynomial a separate within-step approximation and defers its order analysis; a constant or linear polynomial is allowed when coefficients vanish.
def-heun-quadratic-dense-output.endpoints: Definition explicitly gives P_n(0)=yn and P_n(1)=YH, matching the initial value and accepted Heun endpoint.
def-heun-quadratic-dense-output.nonempty-choice: The displayed quadratic polynomial uniquely determines the extension from yn,h,K1,K2; no interpolation-node selection is performed.
def-heun-quadratic-dense-output.iff-forward: The Heun extension item specifies a polynomial and its endpoints, not an equivalence between endpoint order and dense-output order.
def-heun-quadratic-dense-output.iff-reverse: An arbitrary polynomial with those endpoints is not asserted to equal this chosen quadratic or possess its later order estimate.

def-validated-residual-tube-certificate.empty: Definition fixes d>=1 and a<T with a finite strictly increasing panel partition; each panel subdivision must cover its endpoints with no gaps, excluding an empty coverage list.
def-validated-residual-tube-certificate.zero: Definition permits zero nonnegative L_j,rho_j,d_j but requires R_j>0 and a strict supersolution margin, and every field/derivative division denominator must exclude zero.
def-validated-residual-tube-certificate.one: Definition allows one state component and a partition with one panel; its squared residual/Jacobian checks then contain the corresponding scalar entries.
def-validated-residual-tube-certificate.degenerate: Definition requires matching stored polynomial/radius endpoints and evaluates residual from those actual coefficients, so rounded or interpolation errors are included rather than silently replaced by exact stages.
def-validated-residual-tube-certificate.endpoints: Definition demands exact endpoint coverage, neighboring polynomial/radius agreement and d0<R0(a), with the separate initial squared-error check.
def-validated-residual-tube-certificate.nonempty-choice: The certificate is a supplied finite rational record of DAGs, panels, boxes and subdivisions; this definition does not assert that an arbitrary ODE has such a record or choose one.
def-validated-residual-tube-certificate.iff-forward: Validated means passing the listed finite rational enclosure conditions, not a biconditional characterization of all accurate or globally existing ODE trajectories.
def-validated-residual-tube-certificate.iff-reverse: Existence of an exact trajectory or a small reconstruction error is not asserted to imply success of this particular outward interval certificate.

rem-fixed-mesh-global-error-does-not-cer.empty: The Scope warning compares a supplied prescribed uniform mesh with a supplied accepted adaptive run; it offers no new assertion for an empty IVP or missing time mesh.
rem-fixed-mesh-global-error-does-not-cer.zero: The Scope warning identifies absent defect-reliability and variable-step propagation hypotheses, without dividing by a defect or pair difference that might vanish.
rem-fixed-mesh-global-error-does-not-cer.one: A one-step adaptive run still needs the fixed-mesh theorem's actual defect and stability hypotheses; reducing the step count does not provide them.
rem-fixed-mesh-global-error-does-not-cer.degenerate: The Scope warning allows application to a particular adaptive run only after the separate mesh/defect/propagation hypotheses are independently proved.
rem-fixed-mesh-global-error-does-not-cer.endpoints: The Scope warning does not add a horizon-endpoint rule; the contrast is prescribed uniform steps versus variable state-dependent accepted steps.
rem-fixed-mesh-global-error-does-not-cer.nonempty-choice: This scope remark neither constructs a selector nor invokes a choice axiom; it distinguishes the hypotheses of two already supplied numerical interfaces.
rem-fixed-mesh-global-error-does-not-cer.iff-forward: The warning denies an automatic transfer of a fixed-mesh conclusion to adaptivity; it is not an equivalence criterion for adaptive convergence.
rem-fixed-mesh-global-error-does-not-cer.iff-reverse: Failure to obtain a certificate from that fixed-mesh theorem is not a claim that the adaptive trajectory is inaccurate or cannot be certified another way.

thm-bounded-adaptive-runge-kutta-control.empty: Proof step 1.1 retains the controller's accepted prefix; the underlying Definition always includes initial data and can return before any attempted step at a zero horizon.
thm-bounded-adaptive-runge-kutta-control.zero: Proof step 1.1 propagates the defined trial/status branches, including the controller's separate Q=0 proposal case; zero estimator is not used as a divisor.
thm-bounded-adaptive-runge-kutta-control.one: Proof step 2.1 visits indices1 through N and returns on the Nth attempt if no earlier status occurs; N=1 is included in this finite initial-segment argument.
thm-bounded-adaptive-runge-kutta-control.degenerate: Proof step 1.1 sends undefined/nonfinite stages to failure and minimum-step rejection to its stated status, so termination does not presume a successful trajectory.
thm-bounded-adaptive-runge-kutta-control.endpoints: Proof step 2.1 explicitly preserves success when the last funded attempt reaches T; the success check precedes the attempt-budget-exhausted branch.
thm-bounded-adaptive-runge-kutta-control.nonempty-choice: The finite attempt indices and fixed terminal branches in proof steps1.1–2.1 do not select an infinite family of step sizes or require a choice axiom.
thm-bounded-adaptive-runge-kutta-control.iff-forward: This result proves finite termination with one of four statuses, not an equivalence between budget sufficiency and attaining the final time.
thm-bounded-adaptive-runge-kutta-control.iff-reverse: Successful integration is not assumed merely because the controller terminates; failure and safeguard statuses are part of the conclusion.

thm-heun-euler-pair-local-orders-and-est.empty: Statement uses d>=1 and a compact convex starting/stage neighborhood containing the actual initial point; this is not an empty set of starting data.
thm-heun-euler-pair-local-orders-and-est.zero: Proof step 3.1 treats g=0 separately and withholds the ratio-one conclusion; no norm of g is divided out in that branch.
thm-heun-euler-pair-local-orders-and-est.one: Proof steps1.1–2.1 apply Taylor componentwise and include a one-dimensional ODE, with the same time derivative and scalar state derivative in g.
thm-heun-euler-pair-local-orders-and-est.degenerate: Proof step 3.1 keeps the defect orders when g vanishes but states that the estimator ratio does not follow; bounded common derivatives and a common admissible h0 remain required for uniformity.
thm-heun-euler-pair-local-orders-and-est.endpoints: Statement restricts to sufficiently small positive h and exact/stage points inside the open neighborhood; proof step1.1 expands from the given start along that admitted segment.
thm-heun-euler-pair-local-orders-and-est.nonempty-choice: The short solution segment and fixed two-stage outputs are supplied; the componentwise Taylor remainder estimates use finite-dimensional bounds rather than a choice function.
thm-heun-euler-pair-local-orders-and-est.iff-forward: The local-order result gives asymptotic expansions under C2 bounds and one sufficient nonvanishing coefficient for ratio one; it is not an order characterization of arbitrary pairs.
thm-heun-euler-pair-local-orders-and-est.iff-reverse: Observed ratio one or second-order Heun error is not claimed to recover the common compact-neighborhood or bounded-derivative hypotheses.

lem-rational-expression-derivative-recur.empty: Proof step1.1 starts with constant/input nodes in the supplied finite acyclic expression graph; the Statement concerns a represented field, not an empty rootless syntax tree.
lem-rational-expression-derivative-recur.zero: Proof step2.1 forms the quotient derivative only where v is nonzero; continuity first supplies a neighborhood excluding zero, so its v^2 denominator is legitimate.
lem-rational-expression-derivative-recur.one: Proof step1.1 includes a graph with a single constant or coordinate root, whose derivative is the prescribed zero or coordinate derivative without parent recursion.
lem-rational-expression-derivative-recur.degenerate: Proof step1.1 gives derivative zero to constant nodes, and step3.1 permits zero derivative bounds; no nonzero field rank or Jacobian is required.
lem-rational-expression-derivative-recur.endpoints: The Statement restricts to an open neighborhood where every denominator remains nonzero; proof step3.1 shrinks a ball inside that domain, with no assertion at a pole.
lem-rational-expression-derivative-recur.nonempty-choice: Proof step1.1 orders a finite DAG topologically and step3.1 takes bounds for finitely many derivatives; it does not choose values from an arbitrary infinite family.
lem-rational-expression-derivative-recur.iff-forward: The rational-recursion lemma proves that the prescribed node rules compute a derivative on the admitted domain; it gives no biconditional about all differentiable functions.
lem-rational-expression-derivative-recur.iff-reverse: A locally Lipschitz function need not be represented by this rational DAG, and no converse representation claim is stated.

thm-heun-dense-output-local-order-two.empty: Statement fixes one admitted Heun initial value and a nonempty parameter interval0<=theta<=1; it is not a supremum over an empty interpolation set.
thm-heun-dense-output-local-order-two.zero: Proof step1.1 allows zero g or K2-K1; step2.1 compares Taylor remainders without dividing by either coefficient or by theta.
thm-heun-dense-output-local-order-two.one: Proof step2.1 works componentwise for a scalar ODE, while theta=1 selects the single accepted Heun endpoint.
thm-heun-dense-output-local-order-two.degenerate: Proof step2.1 bounds |theta h|^3 by h^3, so zero theta or vanishing Taylor terms require no separate inverse or nondegeneracy assumption.
thm-heun-dense-output-local-order-two.endpoints: Proof steps1.1–2.1 use0<=theta^2<=1 and |theta h|^3<=h^3 uniformly, including theta=0 and theta=1.
thm-heun-dense-output-local-order-two.nonempty-choice: The fixed quadratic and exact short trajectory are compared by Taylor's formula with common derivative bounds; no mesh-dependent arbitrary selector is introduced.
thm-heun-dense-output-local-order-two.iff-forward: The dense-output theorem supplies a uniform local upper bound for this extension, not an equivalence between endpoint and within-step accuracy.
thm-heun-dense-output-local-order-two.iff-reverse: A small endpoint defect alone is not asserted to imply this dense-output estimate; its smoothness and bounded-stage assumptions are inherited explicitly.

alg-validated-residual-tube-certificate-.empty: Definition step1 structurally rejects gaps and endpoint mismatches in the supplied mesh/subdivision, so a missing coverage list cannot pass by vacuous range tests.
alg-validated-residual-tube-certificate-.zero: Definition step4 requires denominator intervals to exclude zero and radius/margin lower endpoints to be strictly positive; zero residual bounds remain permitted when their squared tests pass.
alg-validated-residual-tube-certificate-.one: Definition loops over each supplied finite panel/cell and coordinate, so one panel or one state coordinate merely makes those loops singleton.
alg-validated-residual-tube-certificate-.degenerate: Definition step3 maps nonfinite/domain/split/overflow statuses to inconclusive and step5 reports the first failed check, rather than certifying a partial enclosure.
alg-validated-residual-tube-certificate-.endpoints: Definition step4 checks exact cell coverage and neighboring reconstruction/radius endpoints and performs the separate initial squared-error and strict radius comparison.
alg-validated-residual-tube-certificate-.nonempty-choice: All subdivisions and rational expressions are supplied; the checker performs no automatic subdivision or unbounded search and does not select a certificate for arbitrary data.
alg-validated-residual-tube-certificate-.iff-forward: This finite procedure defines passing and inconclusive statuses; its soundness is a separate theorem and no converse completeness criterion is asserted.
alg-validated-residual-tube-certificate-.iff-reverse: A sound exact trajectory need not be certifiable by the supplied finite interval record, so the algorithm does not identify inconclusive with inaccuracy or nonexistence.

thm-validated-residual-tube-certificate-.empty: Proof step1.1 uses the structurally validated partition/boxes from the checker; the accepted certificate covers the full interval rather than an empty panel family.
thm-validated-residual-tube-certificate-.zero: Proof step1.1 requires all division denominators away from zero and d0<R0(a); step3.1 allows zero initial error or residual but retains a strictly positive supersolution gap.
thm-validated-residual-tube-certificate-.one: Proof step2.1's rowwise Cauchy-Schwarz and squared Frobenius bound apply to one scalar row/column, and step3.1 permits a single panel.
thm-validated-residual-tube-certificate-.degenerate: Proof step3.1 proves a no-first-exit statement using the positive radius gap; step4.1 uses actual compact boxes inside the field domain, not an assumed global ODE existence conclusion.
thm-validated-residual-tube-certificate-.endpoints: Proof step3.1 matches reconstruction/radius values across panel nodes; step4.1 excludes a maximal endpoint before or at T by the compact-tube extension lemma.
thm-validated-residual-tube-certificate-.nonempty-choice: The certificate data are supplied finite rational records, and proof steps3.1–4.1 compose actual local/maximal ODE and finite-panel arguments without claiming selection of a certificate for every field.
thm-validated-residual-tube-certificate-.iff-forward: The soundness theorem states certified implies a unique exact solution in the strict tube; it is not an equivalence between solvability and certification.
thm-validated-residual-tube-certificate-.iff-reverse: Neither a failed enclosure nor an inconclusive checker result is asserted to prove nonexistence of the exact solution or failure of another possible certificate.

thm-validated-residual-tube-checker-term.empty: Statement covers every finite input record; proof step1.1 includes structural validation, so a missing required graph/panel array returns inconclusive rather than starting an unbounded search.
thm-validated-residual-tube-checker-term.zero: Proof step2.1 invokes finite interval operations returning either an enclosure or a declared status; a zero-containing denominator is such a finite failed-operation route, not a nonterminating division.
thm-validated-residual-tube-checker-term.one: Proof step1.1 visits each acyclic node finitely often, including a single-node graph; step2.1 similarly covers a single panel/cell.
thm-validated-residual-tube-checker-term.degenerate: Proof step2.1 ends on either a passing or a failed check, so malformed or noncertifying input need not meet the soundness theorem's certified premise to terminate.
thm-validated-residual-tube-checker-term.endpoints: The termination Statement contains no asymptotic time endpoint; all panels/cells are an already supplied finite record and no automatic subdivision is performed.
thm-validated-residual-tube-checker-term.nonempty-choice: Proof steps1.1–2.1 traverse finite syntax and numerical lists in fixed order, with no infinite search for a successful rational subdivision.
thm-validated-residual-tube-checker-term.iff-forward: The checker termination result asserts finite return for every finite record, not a criterion equating finite return with a successful enclosure.
thm-validated-residual-tube-checker-term.iff-reverse: Its two statuses certified and inconclusive both terminate; termination is never used as a converse proof that the record passes its mathematical inequalities.

ex-below-roundoff-tolerance-breaks-embed.empty: Example specifies one scalar IVP and exactly one funded step with accepted mesh containing its initial pair; it has no empty sample or zero-stage data.
ex-below-roundoff-tolerance-breaks-embed.zero: Verification step1.1 computes identical stored endpoints8 and hence Q=0/(1/4)=0; step2.1 compares this zero estimator with the nonzero true error1.
ex-below-roundoff-tolerance-breaks-embed.one: Example sets attempt budget N=1 and h=1; verification step1.1 accepts the sole trial and the exact endpoint comparison in step2.1 remains9 versus8.
ex-below-roundoff-tolerance-breaks-embed.degenerate: Verification step1.1 applies the explicit tie-to-even rule at9 between8 and10, so the failure of reliability is due to the prescribed rounding, not an undefined computation.
ex-below-roundoff-tolerance-breaks-embed.endpoints: Example reaches T=1 on its only attempt; verification step2.1 evaluates the exact endpoint y(1)=9 and the stored endpoint8.
ex-below-roundoff-tolerance-breaks-embed.nonempty-choice: The toy representable numbers and tie rule fix both stored endpoint values; no random rounding or selection among equal candidates remains unspecified.
ex-below-roundoff-tolerance-breaks-embed.iff-forward: The example exhibits one accepted inaccurate rounded step; it does not state a biconditional characterization of every below-resolution tolerance failure.
ex-below-roundoff-tolerance-breaks-embed.iff-reverse: The example does not infer that every zero embedded difference is inaccurate; it only refutes the general acceptance-as-certificate inference with these exact values.

ex-fast-decay-problem-rejects-at-minimum.empty: Example supplies a scalar start y(0)=1 and two attempted steps; verification steps1.1–2.1 keep the initial state when both trials are rejected.
ex-fast-decay-problem-rejects-at-minimum.zero: Verification steps1.1–2.1 divide by the fixed positive atol=10^-4 and obtain Q=80000 and20000, so no zero estimator denominator or zero trial size is used.
ex-fast-decay-problem-rejects-at-minimum.one: The ODE has one coordinate; verification step2.1 ends after a second trial at the positive minimum step rather than asserting success from a scalar problem.
ex-fast-decay-problem-rejects-at-minimum.degenerate: Verification step2.1 invokes the minimum-step-rejected status at h_min=0.002; the Example explicitly withholds any general stiffness diagnosis from these rejections.
ex-fast-decay-problem-rejects-at-minimum.endpoints: Verification step1.1 first tries the full horizon0.004, then step2.1 rejects at h_min0.002; the safeguard is tested before the attempt budget is reported exhausted.
ex-fast-decay-problem-rejects-at-minimum.nonempty-choice: The supplied safety factor and clamps determine the second proposal exactly; the witness involves no adaptive choice among unspecified meshes.
ex-fast-decay-problem-rejects-at-minimum.iff-forward: The fast-decay example verifies this pair of explicit rejections only and expressly does not equate minimum-step rejection with stiffness.
ex-fast-decay-problem-rejects-at-minimum.iff-reverse: No converse says every stiff equation or every positive minimum step must cause this safeguard; the conclusion is the displayed finite calculation.

ex-heun-euler-estimator-leading-term-van.empty: Example supplies one scalar initial state and one positive step; the two-stage Euler-Heun witness does not range over an empty collection of solutions.
ex-heun-euler-estimator-leading-term-van.zero: Verification step1.1 has K1=YE=0 and step2.1 has zero h^2 leading coefficient; the norm ratio divides by h^3/3>0 because h>0.
ex-heun-euler-estimator-leading-term-van.one: Verification step1.1 is an actual single-step scalar calculation with K2=h^2 and exact integral h^3/3, not a statement about repeated adaptive attempts.
ex-heun-euler-estimator-leading-term-van.degenerate: Verification step2.1 retains the vanishing nominal leading coefficient yet computes ratio3/2, giving the concrete counterexample to extending the nonzero-coefficient rule.
ex-heun-euler-estimator-leading-term-van.endpoints: The Example requires h>0 and its ratio is3/2 on that whole punctured interval; no undefined defect ratio at h=0 is claimed.
